Porsche Motorsport. 
From racing to everything we are.

items.title: Porsche 356 SL
items.subtitle: First class victory in Le Mans
items.description: The 356 SL was the first Porsche entered into racing and in 1951 achieved its first class victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans. Its lightweight design proved successful with many more wins in the years that followed.

items.title: Porsche 550 Spyder
items.subtitle: Panamericana
items.description: In 1954, the first Porsche built especially for racing is a mid‑engine sports car with an aluminium body. It becomes a stand‑out, earning a class victory and a third-place overall ranking in the Carrera Panamericana against higher-capacity competitors.

items.title: Porsche 917KH
items.subtitle: Salzburg
items.description: Arguably one of the most iconic Porsche racing models ever, the 917KH secured its place in history by achieving Porsche’s first overall win at the legendary 24 Hours of Le Mans wearing its iconic red and white Salzburg striped livery.

items.title: Porsche 911 3.0 SC
items.subtitle: East African Safari
items.description: The East African Safari Rally pushes both drivers and cars to the limit. To compete sucessfully, Porsche modifies a 911 by reinforcing the chassis and the body, making a thicker aluminium floor, and raising ground clearance to 28 centimeters.

items.title: Porsche 956
items.subtitle: Group C
items.description: Altered to compete in the newly created Group C (Sports Prototype) class, the 956 was a great success with its highlight coming in the 1982 24 Hours of Le Mans where the car locked out the podium, taking first, second and third.

items.title: Porsche 911 GT1
items.subtitle: Strong Partnership
items.description: The Porsche 911 GT1 went through three iterations between 1996 and 1998 with its most iconic being the 1998 Mobil1 liveried version. While 1997 was a difficult year, 1998 saw Porsche AG finished 1st and 2nd at the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

items.title: Porsche 919 Hybrid LMP1
items.subtitle: Serial Winner
items.description: For the first time in many years, Porsche returned to racing with a Factory team. Between 2014 and 2017, the 919 Hybrid won 17 races and three World Endurance Championships in as many years.

items.title: Porsche 911 RSR
items.subtitle: The Pink Pig
items.description: Two 911 RSR kitted out in historic decor came to the start line at the 2018 Le Mans 24-hour race. In the GT-Pro class, the Porsche 911 RSR "Sau" finishes the race in first place after 344 laps.

items.title: Porsche 963
items.subtitle: Butterfly
items.description: To celebrate 75 years of Porsche and the 100th edition of Le Mans, the Porsche 963 raced in a special “Butterfly” livery in 2023. Its seven historic colors paid tribute to iconic Porsche race cars and Le Mans victories.

car.name: Porsche 963
car.description: The Porsche 963 is the latest in a long line of prototype racecars from the brand. It’s a car that, in its various iterations, has been very successful, most recently, winning the 24 Hours of Daytona for the third year in a row. Weighing just over a ton with 680 horsepower and high downforce. It’s a purebred race car built with one purpose in mind – winning.
car.power: Engine power output: Circa 500 kW (680 PS) @ 8360 1/min. Combined power output: Up to 520 kW at rear axle (Pending on BOP)
car.transmission: Single specification hybrid system, 7-speed racing transmission, pneumatically actuated

Brakes
items.subtitle: Built to brake late.
items.description: Carbon brakes, brake-by-wire technology and optimized cooling ensure consistent stopping power, precise modulation, and maximum confidence deep into every braking zone.

items.title: Cockpit
items.subtitle: Mission Control.
items.description: A purpose-built cockpit designed around the driver. Advanced displays, intuitive controls and race-critical data provide instant access to every performance parameter.

items.title: The Engine
items.subtitle: Hybrid performance.
items.description: Powered by a water-cooled 4.6-litre twin-turbo V8 producing around 680 hp. Single Specification Hybrid System, MGU (Motor Generator Unit) at the rear axle with Lithium-Ionen ESS (Energy Storage System).

items.title: Drive/Power transmission
items.subtitle: Precision-engineered power transfer.
items.description: A seven-speed racing transmission and advanced hybrid integration ensure seamless power delivery, maximizing traction, responsiveness, and endurance performance. Inspired by decades of Porsche motorsport innovation.

items.title: Chassis
items.subtitle: Lightweight. Rigid. Race-ready.
items.description: The carbon-fiber chassis forms the backbone of the Porsche 963, providing exceptional structural stiffness, optimized weight distribution, and a platform built for endurance racing.

items.title: Suspension
items.subtitle: Precision under Pressure.
items.description: Double-wishbone pushrod suspension and race-bred damping deliver exceptional stability, precise feedback, and maximum control at the limit. Inspired by endurance racing, refined for victory.

car.name: Porsche 99X Electric
car.description: A legacy built on speed. A future painted bold. Having made its electrifying debut in Season 11 of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship, the GEN3 Evo Porsche 99X Electric continues to leverage cutting-edge advances—making it the fastest accelerating FIA single-seater race car. Rocketing from 0 to 60 mph / 100 km/h in approx. 2 seconds, it remains an astounding 30% quicker than current F1 cars. This leap in acceleration sets new benchmarks in electric racing technology and performance.

items.title: Bodywork
items.subtitle: Lightweight body.
items.description: The revised aero package, including new louvres above the front wheel arches and a 4 mm Gurney flap on the swan-neck rear wing, reduces pitch sensitivity and enhances aerodynamic behavior – especially in traffic and under variable conditions.

items.title: Cockpit
items.subtitle: Advanced cockpit technology.
items.description: Inside, it’s all about efficiency and focus. Enhanced functions on the steering wheel and improved cockpit ventilation make the 911 GT3 R a place to perform for any driver.

items.title: Suspension
items.subtitle: Precision starts here.
items.description: Optimized suspension kinematics in the front increase anti-dive under braking to improve platform stability. At the rear, modified multi-link geometry increases anti-squat under acceleration.

items.title: The Engine
items.subtitle: Pure Flat-Six Power.
items.description: At its core: a 4.2-liter naturally aspirated flat-six engine, delivering up to 416 kW (565 PS), depending on BoP. The six speed sequential dog-type gearbox ensures fast, aggressive shifts.

items.title: Transmission
items.subtitle: Fast shifts. Maximum traction.
items.description:
The sixspeed sequential dog-type gearbox ensures fast, aggressive shifts. New ceramic wheel bearings in the rear, 
improved driveshaft cooling via NACA ducts, and enhanced steering fluid cooling all contribute to long-term 
durability.

items.title: Brake System
items.subtitle: Maximum control under pressure.
items.description: Designed for uncompromising control, the braking system features advanced Race ABS, two separate brake circuits with brake pressure sensors for the front and rear axles, adjustable by the driver via a balance bar system.

car.name: Technical Specs
car.description: Every line of its bodywork is shaped by purpose – from the three-piece front lip to the swan-neck rear wing. Louvres in the fenders breathe out air, while the underbody and turning vanes carve the air with surgical intent. This isn’t just a race car. It’s a scalpel for the track. And when you’re threading it through a street circuit or diving into a high-speed corner, you’ll feel it: the front axle biting harder, the car responding sharper. This is where aerodynamic evolution meets raw driver instinct.

Bodywork
items.subtitle: Aluminum-steel composite design.
items.description: Every line is shaped by purpose – from the three-piece front lip to the swan-neck rear wing. Louvres in the fenders breathe out air, while the underbody and turning vanes carve the air with surgical intent.

items.title: Interior
items.subtitle: It's all business.
items.description: A new multifunction steering wheel puts more control at your fingertips. Dedicated switches, more clarity. A new display touch panel unlocks deep settings without a laptop – because when seconds count, simplicity wins.

items.title: Suspension
items.subtitle: Built for performance.
items.description: Stiffness-optimized forged control arms and top mounts deliver precise handling. Featuring dust-protected spherical bearings, center-lock wheel hubs, adjustable anti-roll bars, and tire monitoring.

items.title: The Engine
items.subtitle: Naturally aspirated.
items.description: Unfiltered feeling of a 4.0-liter flat-six that screams to 9,000 rpm, now with 520 HP. No turbos. No excuses. Just throttle, revs, and the kind of mechanical honesty that rewards the brave. With individual throttle bodies and longer valve lift.

items.title: Modified 911 cockpit
items.subtitle: Driver-focused.
items.description: Innovative motorsport cockpit combining recyclated-carbon-fiber fleece, ergonomic display touch panel, advanced safety systems, and race-proven functionality.

items.title: Brake System
items.subtitle: Consistent and relentless.
items.description: Wider discs, better cooling, and a brake system that’s been reengineered for durability. The braking system is delivering all the feedback you'll need. Greater friction surface and a new steering setup that tightens your turning radius.
